title: Pear's Bankruptcy, After Payers Would Not Fund Its Prescription Apps
dek: In April 2023 the maker of the first FDA-cleared prescription apps filed for bankruptcy, and its founder said evidence had not been enough to get insurers to pay.

story.event: Filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after payers were slow to reimburse prescription digital therapeutics
story.summary: On 7 April 2023 Pear Therapeutics, the Boston maker of FDA-cleared prescription apps for addiction and insomnia founded by Corey McCann in 2013, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and laid off about 170 people, 92% of its full-time staff, after 2022 revenue of $10.4 million fell far short of its forecast. McCann, who stepped down the day before, said payers could deny payment for therapies that were effective and cost-saving. The assets sold at auction in May 2023 for about $6 million.
paragraphs: On Thursday 6 April 2023 Corey McCann stepped down as chief executive of Pear Therapeutics, the Boston company he had founded in 2013. The next day Pear filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware and let go about 170 people, 92% of its full-time staff, with two weeks' salary as severance. About 15 stayed to run a sale. Pear stopped accepting new prescriptions and said it could not guarantee that existing patients would keep access.

Pear made software that doctors prescribe like a drug. Its reSET, for substance use disorder, had in 2017 become the first digital therapeutic cleared by the FDA; reSET-O, for opioid use disorder, and Somryst, for insomnia, followed. Pear raised more than $400 million in venture funding and in December 2021 went public through a SPAC deal that valued it at $1.6 billion.

The difficulty was payment. In March 2022 McCann told investors that most coverage so far had come through pharmacy benefits, and Pear forecast $22 million of revenue for the year. Progress with commercial and government payers was slow. By midyear the forecast had been cut to between $14 million and $16 million; Pear restructured in July and cut more than a fifth of its staff in November. Revenue for 2022 came to $10.4 million, mostly from agreements with state agencies. In March 2023 it said it was exploring a sale or merger, and might otherwise have to restructure or liquidate.

In a LinkedIn post McCann wrote, "This is certainly not the outcome I envisioned when I founded Pear in 2013." The company had shown, he said, that clinicians would prescribe its products and that they could save payers money. "But that isn't enough," he wrote. "Payors have the ability to deny payment for therapies that are clinically necessary, effective, and cost-saving." He also blamed two hard years for growth-stage companies.

In May the assets were sold at auction to four buyers for about $6 million, against debts of about $32 million; Pear had told shareholders to expect little or no recovery. A new company led by McCann, Harvest Bio, bid about $2 million for reSET, reSET-O and Pear's pipeline. Harvest later sold the two addiction apps to PursueCare, a telehealth provider, which brought them back into use in 2024.

quote.text: The pilot has promised you, not a prosperous voyage, but a serviceable performance of his task—that is, an expert knowledge of steering a ship.
quote.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius (Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium)
quote.locator: Letter LXXXV, "On Some Vain Syllogisms", section 33
quote.source_title: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 85, tr. Richard M. Gummere (Wikisource)
quote.connection: Seneca separates the pilot's skill from the luck of the voyage. McCann's farewell drew the same line: the apps were cleared, prescribed and, he said, able to save money, but whether anyone paid for them was decided by others.

reflection: Seneca's pilot is judged by how he steers, not by whether the sea lets him reach port. Pear's apps did what the regulator asked of them; the people who would have to pay were a separate sea, and it did not open in time. Neither fact cancels the other, and the 170 people who left that Friday carried the cost of both.

You may be doing careful work that nobody has yet agreed to pay for, or to thank you for. It helps to keep two ledgers: one for whether the work is sound, one for whether it is landing. Tired days blur them into one.
invitation: Take one piece of work that has not landed. On one line, write whether it is sound; on another, what is stopping it from being used or paid for. Leave the second line until tomorrow.

research_notes: Figures agree closely across sources. Revenue ($10.4 million for 2022 against initial guidance of $22 million, cut to $14-16 million) comes from MedTech Dive and its sister sites, citing Pear's filings; HLTH and MedTech Dive independently report that slow payer progress forced the lower forecast. McCann's post is dated 8 April by HLTH, but pharmaphorum quoted it on 7 April, so the story gives no date for it. HLTH prints 'prescription digital therapeutics' where Coverager prints 'PDTs', so that sentence is paraphrased. Layoffs: about 170 (8-K, which gives 92% of full-time employees; MedTech Dive; HLTH) with about 15 retained. Earlier cuts: MedTech Dive says 'more than a fifth' in November 2022; pharmaphorum gives about 22% (about 59 people) with third-quarter results; consistent. Funding: Coverager $409 million in eight rounds; pharmaphorum 'more than $400 million'; the story uses the latter. Auction: STAT and pharmaphorum give about $6 million (pharmaphorum's breakdown: $3.9 million Nox Health, about $2 million Harvest Bio, $70,000 Click, $50,000 Welt) against about $32 million of debt; STAT's wording is ambiguous about the per-buyer split, so the story gives only the total. A court hearing to approve the sale was set for 22 May 2023; pharmaphorum (October 2024) reports Harvest Bio as owner and later seller of reSET and reSET-O, which implies approval, but the hearing outcome itself was not read, so the story says only that Harvest 'bid' and 'later sold'. The PursueCare sale is dated 'last December' (December 2023) by pharmaphorum; the story says only 'later' and that the apps returned in 2024. McCann's LinkedIn post was not available directly; its wording is taken from passages printed identically by pharmaphorum, Coverager and Behavioral Health Business (BH Business prints '[Payers]' for 'Payors'). The causes stated are McCann's own (payers, market conditions); MedTech Dive's reporting of slow payer progress is given as reporting. The SEC pages were fetched without any personal details in the request. The Seneca passage contrasts the pilot's art with the voyage's success; a few lines later Seneca grants that the pilot's passengers can still be harmed, which the reflection reflects.
